clue.text: Survive within elite mostly getting source of credit

indicators.note: within says one piece is put inside the other
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is the elite
to last is to survive or endure

explanation.surface: Someone getting by among the privileged, mostly on borrowed money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of credit' is a nickname for a card, not a bank; 'elite' is a noun here, the pick of the bunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A credit card is commonly called plastic, so it is a source of credit.

clue.text: Taste shown by veneer covering article

indicators.note: covering says the outer piece wraps round the other

parts.note: plate is a thin coating of metal, a veneer
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Good taste shown by putting a thin facing over a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's palate is their sense of taste, as in a refined palate.

clue.text: Welcome statute stifling church power

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the outer word holds the others inside

parts.note: an act is a statute passed by parliament
CE is the Church of England
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A welcome law that curbs the influence of the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something is to receive it gladly, to welcome it.

clue.text: It permits a new mood in the group

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A rule change permitting a fresh atmosphere among colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like an adjective on 'mood' but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Team spirit is the shared morale and camaraderie of a group.

clue.text: Arranged credit, mainly for drink

indicators.note: arranged means put in order, so the letters are reordered
mainly means most of the word, so its final letter goes

explanation.surface: A loan set up chiefly to buy alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims CREDIT to CREDI, which 'Arranged' reorders.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is an alcoholic drink made from fermented apples.

clue.text: Women must have complete authority

parts.note: arrant means complete or utter, as in an arrant fool

explanation.surface: A demand that women be given total power.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrant is a document or right giving official authority to act.

clue.text: One from Los Angeles perhaps seen in type of film genre regularly

parts.note: a western is a cowboy film

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Hollywood resident spotted in a cowboy picture now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd and 4th letters of 'genre', ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Los Angeles is in the western USA, so someone from there is an example of a western person.

clue.text: Swim in river with fish

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A swim in the river among the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swim' is not about water: when your head swims, it whirls.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to feel dizzy and spin, as a head swims.

clue.text: Drunk — and a rich web designer

indicators.note: drunk means tipsy and staggering, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wealthy, tipsy designer of websites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'web designer' sounds like a website builder, but it means a spider, which designs webs.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider is an arachnid, and spiders spin and design webs.

clue.text: Going off after short time horse-riding?

indicators.note: after says the second piece follows the first

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, shortened
food going off is rotting

explanation.surface: Setting out on a ride after only a brief wait.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that trotting is one gait of riding, a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Trotting is riding a horse at a moderate two-beat gait.

clue.text: Eventually, crash-test will expose material

indicators.note: will expose says the letters are on show inside these words, waiting to be uncovered

explanation.surface: A car safety test will reveal what something is really made of, sooner or later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eventually' looks like a last-letters signal, but it simply supplies the start of the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is a stretchy synthetic fabric, so a material.

clue.text: Outlaw lost speed — runs with difficulty

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have gone astray and are in disarray

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
ado means fuss or trouble, as in without further ado

explanation.surface: A bandit's getaway falters as he slows and struggles to run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges SPEED to DESPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless bandit or criminal, a Wild West outlaw.

clue.text: Textiles requiring efforts to contain a bug

indicators.note: to contain says the first piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: tries are attempts or efforts
a pest is an insect or bug

explanation.surface: Fabric hangings needing work to keep an insect out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapestries are woven decorative fabrics, a kind of textile.

clue.text: Talk daily needing time for resistance

indicators.note: needing introduces the change that the cleaner word requires
for here means in place of, so one letter swaps for another

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British word for a domestic cleaner who comes in each day
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A newspaper needs time to resist something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' is not a newspaper but a CHAR, a British cleaning lady; T replaces its R.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat is to talk informally.

clue.text: States accepted by worn-out horses having these on their backs

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in by, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: hacks are tired, worked-out horses
avers means states or declares

explanation.surface: Tired horses carrying packs, by general agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: these are what the hacks have on their backs.
explanation.definitionFit: Haversacks are canvas bags carried on the back, which the riders or packhorses bear.

clue.text: Detective with feeling about pressure for immunity

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: about says one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: a sensation is a feeling
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A detective with a hunch, under pressure, seeking an exemption.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispensation is an exemption from a rule, a form of immunity.

clue.text: Poor writer on novel losing head

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a pen is something that writes

indicators.note: losing head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: curious means strange or novel

explanation.surface: An impoverished author whose new book has lost its opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' is not a book but an adjective, odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Penurious means extremely poor, living in penury.

clue.text: Liking to protect new decking

indicators.note: to protect means to surround and shield, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: adoring means loving or liking

explanation.surface: Fondness for preserving a freshly laid deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decking' is not timber flooring but the verb, to deck out.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a room is to decorate it, so decking means adorning.

clue.text: Succeeded — then folded and made severe economies

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
crimped means pressed into folds or ridges

explanation.surface: A business that did well, then went under and had to cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'folded' suggests a business collapsing; it means pressed into ridges.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to be very sparing with money, cutting costs hard.

clue.text: Sign on delivery for reference books

indicators.note: on says the second piece comes next to the first, following it

parts.note: diction is a speaker's delivery or enunciation
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A signature required when a parcel is handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign on delivery' reads as a courier's instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionaries are standard examples of reference books.

clue.text: Run through new recipe

indicators.note: new says the letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: Going over a freshly devised method of cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run through' suggests rehearsing; it means stabbing with a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone through is to stab them, which is to pierce them.

clue.text: Approved sort of ox put back in old herd every now and then

indicators.note: put back means returned, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a yak is a type of ox

indicators.note: every now and then means taking alternate letters

explanation.surface: An ox returned to an ancient herd was given the nod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every now and then' picks ED from 'herd'.
explanation.definitionFit: Okayed means approved or sanctioned, from saying OK.

clue.text: Attack from journal mostly rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters are read backwards
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal

explanation.surface: An onslaught from a magazine that largely got turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims DIARY to DIAR, which 'rejected' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden assault or attack.

clue.text: Cleaner sort of witchcraft?

parts.note: a sweeping tool that is also what a witch flies on, so a cleaning device and a kind of craft

explanation.surface: A query about a purer or more wholesome kind of magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'witchcraft' splits as witch craft, a vehicle for a witch; 'Cleaner' is a noun, a thing that cleans.
explanation.definitionFit: A brush on a long handle sweeps floors, and folklore has witches riding one.

clue.text: Safe haven from love unchanged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so the letter O
as is means in its present condition, unchanged

explanation.surface: A refuge where love stays constant.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in the desert, and figuratively any place of refuge.

clue.text: Lake Ireland viewed from the south?

indicators.note: in a down clue, viewed from the bottom means read upwards

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A lake in Ireland seen from its southern shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America.

clue.text: Arrogant Independent politician — critical but not initially

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: but not initially means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a serious condition is a critical one

explanation.surface: A haughty independent MP who is grave, though not at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperious means domineering and overbearing, much like arrogant.

clue.text: Whine about universal right for groom

indicators.note: about says the outer piece goes round the others

parts.note: to cry is to whine or wail
U is the film classification for universal

explanation.surface: Someone complaining about the rights of a stable lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' is a verb: to curry a horse is to rub it down with a currycomb.
explanation.definitionFit: To curry a horse is to brush and dress its coat, which is grooming it.

clue.text: Happy without line, understands devices

indicators.note: without means the word lacks the letter that follows

parts.note: glad means happy
gets means understands, as in I get it

explanation.surface: Someone cheerful without a phone line still grasps their gizmos.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadgets are small mechanical or electronic contraptions, so devices.

clue.text: Defer and pay out after American flipped

indicators.note: after says the second piece follows the first
flipped means turned over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: US stands for American, as in US forces
to spend is to pay out money

explanation.surface: Postpone and settle the bill once the American has changed his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to put it off for a while, which is to defer it.
